title: GTA VI Leads The Game Awards With Eight Nominations — Before a Single Player Has Touched It
excerpt: GTA VI leads The Game Awards 2026 with eight nominations, including Game of the Year — announced Nov. 17, one day before the game launches Nov. 19.
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has not been released yet, and it is already the most-nominated game at The Game Awards 2026. The nominees were announced on Tuesday, November 17, in a livestream hosted by the show's creator, Geoff Keighley — and Rockstar Games' return to Vice City walked away with eight nominations, including Game of the Year.

The game does not reach players until Thursday, November 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. It is priced at $79.99 as a single-player game, and it stars Lucia, played by Manni L. Perez, who also earned a Best Performance nomination for the role.

The eight nominations

GTA VI is nominated for Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Performance for Manni L. Perez, and Best Action/Adventure Game. No other game matched its total. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem each earned six nominations, and Phantom Blade Zero earned five.

The Game of the Year field is GTA VI, 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The nominees were chosen by a global jury of more than 160 media and creator outlets, according to the show's official release.

Eligible by a single day

The nominations landed before a single paying player could touch the game — and before any reviews were published. The timing works because of the show's own calendar: games must be commercially available by 9 p.m. Pacific time on Friday, November 20, and GTA VI launches on November 19, clearing the cutoff by one day. Digital store listings unlock the game at midnight Eastern on November 19, which is 9 p.m. Pacific on November 18. The launch date was locked in on November 6, 2025, when Rockstar pushed the game back to November 19, 2026.

Reports in October said Rockstar sent review code to outlets on the voting jury weeks before launch, with the review embargo reportedly lifting on November 18. Winners are decided mostly by the jury, which accounts for 90 percent of the result, with public fan voting making up the remaining 10 percent. Fan voting closes at 6 p.m. Pacific on Wednesday, December 9, and the winners will be announced at the ceremony on Thursday, December 10, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.

What it means

Analysis: The eight nominations are a bet on reputation as much as on a finished game. The jury voted on a title it had not played in full, and the eligibility rules made that possible by design — a one-day window that Rockstar's delay created. Variety has called GTA VI the favorite for Game of the Year, and the nomination count backs that up. But the short runway cuts both ways: voters will have only about three weeks with the finished game before the December 10 ceremony, and if the launch stumbles, the early coronation will look premature. For now, the most anticipated game of the decade arrives tomorrow with the industry's biggest prize already within reach — before anyone outside Rockstar has finished playing it.
